name: ch340g_usb_uart
description: CH340G USB-UART bridge, assembled from four block templates cut out of the golden page. The blocks are placed on a grid of their own — they are NOT put back where the golden had them — which is what makes this a test of assembly rather than a re-encoding.

provenance.note: Task 008a: the templates are board-extracts (source 3 of the three the architecture lists), so this validates the assembly mechanism, not template authoring quality. Template authoring is 008c/d.

blocks.note: Top-left, where the connector physically is. Signal flow leaves it downward.
Top right, in the second column: 238 units of whitespace separate it from the USB block, so the two read as separate circuits — which the golden's tighter packing did not.
Bottom left, below the USB front end it takes D+/D- from. The golden's own top-to-bottom order (input, rail, bridge) is preserved.
Bottom right, downstream of the core it takes RX/TX from.

notes: Every number on this board is a parameter; the spec states all of them so the design does not silently depend on a template default.
The status LED and its series resistor live inside the power block: in the golden they share that block's ground rail, and a boundary drawn between them would cut copper (the cut tool refuses that).
